newsitem.title: USA: Slim arb shuts North Sea crude out of U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Slim arb shuts North Sea crude out of U.S. Gulf.

text.p: The trans-Atlantic arbitrage narrowed sharply on Friday, keeping North Sea crude sellers out of the U.S. Gulf Coast for now, traders said.
Brent crude for end-August delivery into the Gulf was assessed around five to 10 cents under September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, up from minus 15-25 cents on Thursday.
"Next week's dates have really popped up. So far in this short-term window, it's really tight," a U.S. refiner said.
A U.S. company late Thursday sold the last of a series of Brent cargoes at an unconfirmed discount to September WTI/Cushing.
Traders estimated the price anywhere from minus 20 cents to minus 35 cents a barrel.
Earlier suggestions that other companies might bring Brent across the Atlantic faded in light of the sharply narrower arbitrage.
"The arb looks pretty well shut. The numbers don't seem to work right now," a European seller said.
Several West African cargoes, however, were still looking for homes on the Gulf Coast.
A U.S. company was heard offering Nigerian Brass River for August 20-25 delivery, asking around $2.00-2.05 a barrel over Dated Brent.
Other companies were offering Nigerian Bonny Light and Qua Iboe for end-August arrival, each asking around Dated Brent plus $1.90 a barrel, traders said.
A trading house was also heard offering Indonesian Widuri crude off the water, attesting to the continued ready availability of crude despite recent supply woes, including Hurricane Danny.
In Latin America, Occidental said it could restart operations on its Cano Limon field in Colombia pending confirmation that the Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline had suffered no further attacks.
Oxy declared force majeur on the 175,000 barrel per day (bpd) field on July 15.
State oil company Ecopetrol declared force majeure on loadings on July 6.
Elsewhere in the region, a Swiss-based trader on Thursday sold a cargo of Ecuadoran Oriente crude to Exxon for its 22,000 bpd refinery in El Salvador at an undisclosed price.
